title: LatchGitMutationReceiptV2
description: The host's durable record of one Git mutation, scoped to the device that sent it. Every mutation route answers with it (202 while pending, 200 otherwise), and GET /v2/git/receipts/{requestId} returns it later to the same device only. The host writes it as pending before Git runs, so after a lost response or a host restart the phone reads it instead of repeating the action.

state.description: pending: accepted and running, or not yet reconciled. completed: Git did it. rejected: nothing was changed (Git refused, or the state changed since review: code refresh_required). uncertain: the host cannot tell whether Git finished (it was interrupted or timed out and the repository does not settle the question); read the repository before acting again.

code.description: Stable reason: staged, unstaged, committed, branch_created, switched; refresh_required, operation_in_progress, nothing_to_commit, identity_missing, signing_failed, hook_failed, would_overwrite, branch_exists, invalid_branch_name, not_found, git_refused, not_applied; fetched, up_to_date, fast_forwarded, merged, rebased, stopped (Git stopped a merge or rebase; files lists conflicted paths), continued, aborted; not_fast_forward, unresolved_conflicts, conflict_markers, no_operation, no_upstream, remote_not_found, auth_failed, network_failed, local_changes, hook_failed; pushed, up_to_date, already_on_remote; non_fast_forward, remote_rejected, auth_failed, network_failed, remote_not_found, hook_failed, push_unconfirmed (the host cannot tell from this Mac whether the remote accepted a push: check the remote); interrupted, timed_out. Unknown codes are shown by message.

message.description: One plain sentence for the phone to show.

gitOutput.description: Git's own output (stderr then stdout), bounded, for a refusal or failure.

head.description: HEAD's commit after the operation (or at reconciliation).

commit.description: The commit a completed commit created, or the commit a completed push left at the destination.

files.description: Files Git named in a refusal, such as the local changes a switch would overwrite.

reconciled.description: True when the host decided this outcome by reading the repository after an interruption rather than from Git's exit.

startedAt.description: When Git was started for this request, after the recheck. Absent or null: Git has not been started (or the host predates this field).

progress.description: Git's latest progress line while the request is pending, as last seen by this gateway process. Absent once settled or after a host restart. Progress, and a phone that stops waiting, say nothing about whether Git has stopped.
